q: when the model is held fixed and only the harness varies, how large are the differences a deployer should expect
r: Include: controlled comparison of harnesses with model fixed, repeated trials, cost and failure metrics; contribution is the evaluation method.

q: agents implement a REST API server and modify it across a tunable number of procedurally generated follow-up change requests
r: Include: new multi-turn benchmark where agents build and extend an application over 100 change requests.

q: we introduce ICAE-Bench, an benchmark for evaluating coding agents under interactive project-building settings
r: Include: new benchmark for building repositories from ambiguous product requirements, project level.

q: We introduce LOOPSBENCH, a long horizon benchmark for loop engineering in coding agent evaluation.
r: Include: new long-horizon benchmark with loop-trace metrics, contribution is the evaluation method for sustained development.

q: Results show that the evaluated popular coding agents still struggle to implement user requests in existing repositories
r: EC6: PR-derived issue-resolution benchmark (SWE-bench style) on existing repositories, always excluded.

q: The study synthesizes 164 scholarly works, 100 practitioner records, 29 benchmark records, and 17 author-system case records
r: Include: multivocal review on evaluating coding agents (secondary study, kept), with evaluation design guidance.

q: Recent large language models (LLMs) can operate as coding agents that build complete games from natural language requests.
r: Include: new benchmark of agents building complete games from natural language, project level, with a new evaluation design.

q: we introduce SWE Refactor Bench, a benchmark comprising 20 whole-repository migrations
r: Include: whole-repository long-horizon task with a new three-stage evaluation protocol (method contribution), 520 runs; borderline as migration is not from requirements.

q: This paper presents DeltaSelect, a method that uses repeated published trials to select a small, fixed task set within a specified budget
r: Include: contribution is an evaluation method handling run-to-run variation and cost for comparing coding agents.

q: We introduce GameLogicBench, a benchmark of 72 gameplay-logic tasks in Godot projects.
r: Include: new benchmark with deterministic tick-level evaluator and cost/solve-rate reporting for agents implementing game code in projects.
